summary: ACP's one strong control is the allowance: a delegated token works for one merchant, one session, one use, up to a maximum amount and until an expiry, enforced by the PSP. Everything else is bilateral trust. The merchant authenticates the agent with a bearer token agreed out of band, and the agent verifies webhooks with a shared HMAC secret. Request signatures are only recommended on checkout and contradictory on Delegate Payment, request freshness is a SHOULD, and nothing records that the buyer approved the purchase. Order webhooks are well specified with HMAC and a 300-second window. As of 2026-10-20 no CVE or GitHub advisory exists (advisories API and NVD keyword search), and the published research models ACP formally but reports findings only in aggregate. The practical risks sit in implementations: key handling, card data at PSPs, content injection into the agent and drift between snapshots. At a PCI-attested seller a Stripe SPT can also be resolved once into card credentials, which brings card data back into the seller's scope.

threats.title: Stolen bearer token impersonates an agent
threats.description: The merchant authenticates the agent with a bearer token agreed out of band; the agent verifies the merchant's webhooks with a separate HMAC secret. Anyone holding the agent's token can create and complete sessions as that agent.
preconditions: The key leaks from logs, config or a compromised service
Request signatures are not enforced by the merchant
threats.impact: Fraudulent orders charged to tokens the attacker obtained elsewhere, or reconnaissance of prices and stock.
threats.implementerNotes: Require the detached Signature and Timestamp on every request even though they are only recommended, rotate keys, and allowlist the agent platform's egress IP ranges.

threats.title: Forged order webhook
threats.description: An attacker posts fake order_update events to the agent's webhook to show false shipping, refunds or cancellations to the buyer.
preconditions: The receiver skips Merchant-Signature verification
Or the shared secret leaked
threats.impact: Buyer misinformed; support load; possible social engineering.
threats.implementerNotes: Verify HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a dot and the raw body, reject outside 300 seconds, compare in constant time.

threats.title: Allowance set above the approved total
threats.description: The agent sets max_amount higher than what the buyer confirmed, for example to absorb later changes, so a merchant can charge more than approved.
preconditions: Agent bug or policy that pads the allowance
Merchant changes totals after confirmation
threats.impact: Buyer charged more than approved; dispute.
threats.implementerNotes: Set max_amount to the confirmed total and start a new session when totals change. Stripe tells agents to set max_amount to the transaction total.

threats.title: Totals changed between confirmation and complete
threats.description: The merchant returns new totals on complete or adds fees after the buyer confirmed.
preconditions: No signed record of the confirmed cart
Allowance larger than the new total
threats.impact: Charge differs from what the buyer saw.
threats.implementerNotes: Compare the totals in the complete response with the confirmed totals and cancel when they differ; keep the allowance tight.

threats.title: No proof of what the buyer approved
threats.description: ACP carries no signed user consent. After a dispute, neither merchant nor issuer can prove the buyer approved this purchase. A community issue of 2026-10-15 adds a related gap: a merchant whose PSP adds no field of its own keeps no record of which agent or platform placed the order. A representment then has nothing to point at; no maintainer had replied by 2026-10-20.
preconditions: A buyer disputes an agent purchase
threats.impact: Chargeback outcomes depend on logs of the agent platform and merchant.
threats.implementerNotes: Keep confirmation logs with session id, totals and timestamps; consider Verifiable Intent or AP2-style mandates outside ACP.

threats.title: Card data exposure through direct Delegate Payment
threats.description: PCI DSS Level 1 merchants and PSPs that host Delegate Payment receive raw card numbers and CVC. By 2026-10-20 (absent from the 2026-09-21 capture of the seller page) a seller on another processor can also resolve a granted Stripe SPT once into fpan, network_token, agentic_token or dpan credentials; Stripe encrypts them unless the seller has filed a PCI Attestation of Compliance.
preconditions: Logging of request bodies
Weak vault controls
threats.impact: Card data breach and PCI DSS findings.
threats.implementerNotes: Never log full card numbers or CVC; OpenAI may ask for an attestation of compliance before enabling production access. Treat resolved SPT credentials as cardholder data.

threats.title: Buyer data shared beyond need
threats.description: Checkout sends names, addresses, emails and risk signals such as IP address and device fingerprint to the merchant.
preconditions: Agent sends risk_signals and buyer fields by default
threats.impact: Over-sharing of personal data; consent and data protection exposure.
threats.implementerNotes: Send only the fields the merchant needs; OpenAI says it shares only what the order requires with the user's permission.

threats.title: Markdown or content injection into the agent interface
threats.description: A merchant message or line item description carries raw HTML or instructions that the agent renders or follows.
preconditions: Agent renders merchant content without sanitizing
Model reads merchant text as instructions
threats.impact: Interface spoofing or prompt injection steering the purchase.
threats.implementerNotes: Since 2026-04-17 markdown must be CommonMark without raw HTML; render with raw HTML disabled and treat merchant text as data, not instructions.

threats.title: Idempotency abuse and retry storms
threats.description: Clients retry with new keys or flood with in-flight duplicates, creating duplicate sessions or exhausting the merchant.
preconditions: Client bugs or a malicious agent
No rate limits
threats.implementerNotes: Require Idempotency-Key, return 409 with Retry-After for in-flight keys and 422 for changed bodies; rate limit per key and per agent.

threats.title: Replayed checkout requests
threats.description: Request timestamps are only SHOULD, so a captured signed request may be replayed later if the server does not check freshness.
preconditions: Attacker captures a request
Server skips Timestamp checks
threats.impact: Duplicate side effects where idempotency keys differ.
threats.implementerNotes: Check Timestamp freshness and keep idempotency keys at least 24 hours.

threats.title: Version and schema drift exploited
threats.description: Agents and merchants validate against different snapshots or examples, so fields such as items versus line_items are dropped or misread.
preconditions: Released folders edited after release
Examples do not match the schema
threats.impact: Wrong quantities or failed orders; inconsistent behavior across merchants.
threats.implementerNotes: Pin a commit, validate against the JSON Schema, and test the docs-versus-spec differences explicitly.

scenarios.title: Padded allowance meets a changed cart
preconditions: Agent sets max_amount above the confirmed total
Merchant adds a fee after confirmation
steps: Agent requests a token with max_amount 150 dollars
Merchant returns a total of 130 dollars on complete
PSP accepts the charge because it is inside the allowance
scenarios.impact: Buyer pays 30 dollars more than approved; the only remedy is a refund or a dispute.

scenarios.title: Leaked agent key used for fake orders
preconditions: Agent bearer token leaks
Merchant accepts requests without signatures or IP allowlisting
steps: Attacker creates sessions with the leaked key
Attacker completes them with tokens from stolen cards issued elsewhere
scenarios.impact: Fraud losses on the merchant, which is merchant of record.

scenarios.title: Replayed webhook marks an order refunded
preconditions: Agent receiver checks the HMAC but not the timestamp window
steps: Attacker captures an old order_update with a refund adjustment
Agent shows the buyer a second refund
scenarios.impact: Confusion and support cost; fixed by enforcing the 300-second tolerance.

research.title: A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols
research.finding: Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2: 86 verification cases and 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency findings across the four protocols, not broken down by protocol in the abstract.

research.title: Building Trust in Autonomous Commerce: A Verifiable Global Event Timeline
research.finding: Says protocols such as AP2 and ACP lack interoperable, tamper-evident audit trails.
